header:
Date: 2026-08-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Eve M (Redwood AE), Samir P (Redwood SE), Linda C (Redwood Solutions), Marco R (TundraLink), Priya N (TundraLink CTO), Jonah L (Infra), Asha K (Partnerships)
summary: Intro discovery between Redwood partnerships + TundraLink (SaaS integrator for retail AI). Goals: evaluate channel/reseller fit, pilot scoping for hybrid GPU capacity (APAC focus), security/compliance gating, and initial perf/cost targets. Key blockers: tenancy model, SAML + SSO integration, and minimum committed capacity for dedicated pools.
topics: Private/Dedicated vs hosted fit for reseller customers
Pilot scope, perf benchmarks, and timelines
Security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Eve (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call. I'm Eve, AE on partnerships. Samir's with me from SE.
[00:10] Marco (TundraLink): Hey hi, Marco here, thanks. We're excited to talk through what a channel partnership could look like.
[00:15] Priya (TundraLink CTO): Hi all, quick context — TundraLink runs an analytics SaaS for retail customers in APAC and EMEA, looking to add LLM features but we want to avoid re-building infra.
[00:25] Samir (Redwood SE): Great. We usually see two patterns: you resell hosted API with a margin or operate Dedicated pools for your customers. Either way, we try to keep the developer API consistent.
[00:35] Jonah (Infra): Curious on tenancy — for resold dedicated pools would each customer need an isolated GPU subset or can we do logical separation?
[00:45] Samir: Good question. We support dedicated GPU pools per partner account and you can provision per-tenant instances or multi-tenant routing with strict namespace-level isolation. There are tradeoffs — pure isolation costs more, multi-tenant saves unit costs but needs strict RBAC + encryption per tenant.
[01:05] Marco: When you say "namespace-level" is that compatible with our KMS setup? We use an HSM in our data centres for key material.
[01:12] Samir: Yes, Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, but if you're reselling the hosted API we can also support bring-your-own-key via customer-managed KMS in the VPC path. There are some audit log differences.
[01:28] Priya: Security is table stakes — SOC2 is required, SAML SSO for our customers, and we need per-customer auditability.
[01:35] Eve: We have a SOC2 pack and an example SAML integration guide; I'll share the docs after. I think the bigger ops question is how you want to package it — are you thinking joint go-to-market or pure resale?
[01:46] Asha (Partnerships): Initially pure resale to our existing customers, with co-sell later. We need a competitive margin sheet and an onboarding flow that doesn't force our customers into long infra migrations.
[02:00] Samir: From a pilot perspective, here's a common framing: a 2-week POC with a small dedicated pool (2xA100 equivalent) + routing rules, run a set of representative workloads. We'll provide perf numbers and a small integration checklist.
[02:18] Jonah: For benchmarking — we have mixed seq lengths; a lot of short chat-like prompts and some longer synthesis tasks. Are there model variants you recommend?
[02:28] Samir: Yes — for chat/synthesis we typically suggest a 7B-13B quantized variant to start for lower latency/cost, and then an up-tier to 70B for heavy summarization where quality matters. Also KV cache warmups matter; we can enable prefix caching for frequent prompts.
[02:48] Marco: Sorry, 'K-V cash' was that?
[02:51] Samir: KV cache — key-value cache, sometimes the transcriber makes it funky. It keeps past tokens cached so subsequent tokens are faster.
[03:00] Priya: Cost question — what are ballpark unit costs for resold hosted vs dedicated reserved? We need to model margin at 20-30%.
[03:08] Eve: We'll send a pricing sheet. Hosted pricing is per-token/embedding; Dedicated has a monthly reserved cost + lower per-token units. Typically partners see better margin on Dedicated if they commit.
[03:22] Marco: Timelinewise, our board wants something live in Q4 for two flagship customers, pilot in Aug/Sept ideal.
[03:30] Eve: That's doable. We can aim to get a pilot scoped and signed in Aug, onboarding the first customer in Sept.
[03:38] Samir: Technical gating — for Private deployments we need network diagrams, firewall rules, and an infra contact. For hosted resell we need SSO SAML endpoints and customer onboarding flow.
[03:50] Jonah: For Private/on-prem we have strict egress rules, so will Redwood need outbound to your control plane?
[03:57] Samir: In most Private installs there's a customer-managed control plane with optional telemetry back to Redwood if you enable it. We can do air-gapped deployment but that adds lead time.
[04:08] Priya: How do rollbacks and canary deploys work for partners? If a model update regresses quality for a customer, can we pin versions?
[04:16] Samir: Yes — rollout policies allow pinning and canarying. We also support automatic fallback to a stable model variant when a health check fails.
[04:26] Marco: Any immediate red flags on our side? Our infra is mostly GCP in APAC with some bare-metal for specific retail partners.
[04:33] Samir: That's fine. GCP is well supported; bare-metal is where Private deployment would come in. We should capture a short inventory of your bare-metal specs.
[04:44] Asha: Licensing and revenue share — typical split?
[04:47] Eve: It depends on commit size and go-to-market. We can propose a tiered reseller margin: higher % for multi-year commitments or for Dedicated capacity caps. We'll include options in the SOW.
[05:00] Marco: Can you run a small perf run with our payload? We'll attach traces.
[05:04] Samir: Yes. If you share traces we'll map them to recommended model/quantization profiles and give expected latency/cost per request.
[05:12] Priya: Legal — we'll need an overview of data residency and what logs leave our systems. Also indemnity around outputs; some of our retailers are sensitive to hallucinations.
[05:23] Eve: We'll provide the security FAQ and legal pack. For hallucination controls we recommend guardrails like reranking, eval prompts, and quality monitors — Redwood Optimize can help there.
[05:36] Jonah: A small nit — we prefer JWT-based service accounts rather than long-lived API keys, possible?
[05:41] Samir: Yes, we support short-lived tokens and mTLS service identities in Dedicated/Private modes.
[05:48] Asha: For the pilot SOW, can we include a simple co-marketing clause? If the pilot is successful we'd like a joint case study.
[05:55] Eve: Absolutely — we can draft a lightweight approval flow to protect both sides.
[06:00] Marco: Anything else on the tech side?
[06:03] Samir: Just one operational note — KV cache priming can make POC numbers optimistic; we'll do cold-start and warm-start runs.
[06:10] Marco: Good call.
[06:13] Priya: Ok let's recap.
[06:15] Eve: Recap: Redwood to send pilot SOW + pricing; Samir to send pre-req checklist and provide perf baseline once they get traces; TundraLink to share workload traces and confirm legal owner. Schedule benchmark window Aug 24-28.
[06:29] Marco: Sounds right.
[06:31] Asha: I'll follow up with contract owner and timeline.
[06:34] Eve: Great, I'll send the intro to our partnerships ops and include the SOC2 kit. Expect the email today.
[06:41] Priya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the pilot.
[06:44] Samir: Thanks all.
[06:46] -- End of recording --

Notes:
- Deck referenced: "Redwood Channel Partner Overview" (link shared in chat).
- Quick links promised: SOC2 pack, SAML integration guide, pricing template, pilot SOW template.
- Mentioned potential competitor pressure from CloudHaven and NimbusGrid in APAC — TundraLink wants clarity on margin and SLAs.

Transcription quirks: occasional mis-heard acronyms ("K-V cash" for KV cache), speaker overlap brief at 00:25-00:35.
